newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel breaks 3.4 to the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel breaks 3.4 to the dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed lower against the dollar and the currency basket on Monday amid high activity by the business sector, dealers said.
"Heavy demand for the dollar from the business sector led to another decline of the shekel despite the fact that the dollar was stable in overseas markets," said Guy Levi at Bank Leumi.
"There was no apparent reason for the demand and the trend might change tomorrow," he said.
Levi added that the basket rose to 6.7 percent below the mid-point of its trading bands and the Bank of Israel stayed out of the market.

The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the currency basket, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for three months. The bands are set at seven percent above and below the mid-point.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.4030 shekels against 3.3940 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6761 shekels against 3.6687 on Friday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.6909 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.6937 on Friday, and against the mark at 1.9750 shekels after 1.9735 on Friday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.4030 shekels.
